prompt_text: What is the best health insurance broker in Kansas City MO for someone who is self-employed?
answer_verbatim:
I can help — but “best” depends on your priorities (budget, whether you want ACA marketplace plans and premium tax credits, HSA eligibility, desire for ongoing service, etc.). A few quick questions will let me give specific recommendations:
- Do you need an individual/family plan on the ACA marketplace (with possible premium tax credits), or do you want off‑exchange plans or short‑term coverage?
- Do you have any employees (small-group options) or is it just you?
- What ZIP code or part of Kansas City (MO) are you in?
- Do you want a local in‑person agent or are you fine with an online broker?

While you answer, here are practical, immediate steps and options so you can find a great broker now:

What to look for in a broker
- Independent vs captive: independent brokers represent many carriers and can compare more options; captive agents (State Farm, Allstate, etc.) only sell one carrier.
- Experience with self‑employed clients: ask how many self‑employed/1099 clients they serve.
- Familiarity with ACA marketplace enrollment and subsidies.
- Ongoing service: do they help after enrollment (billing problems, mid‑year plan changes, renewals)?
- Fee structure: most agents are paid by carriers via commission, but ask if they charge extra fees.

Good places to start
- HealthCare.gov (Missouri uses the federal marketplace) if you want subsidized ACA plans and to see eligibility for tax credits.
- National comparison/broker platforms that serve Missouri: eHealth, HealthSherpa, Policygenius — good for quick quotes and comparison.
- Local independent brokers/agencies — often better for hands‑on help and ongoing service. To find and vet them:
  - Search Google Maps for “health insurance broker Kansas City MO” and check reviews.
  - Verify licensing and any complaints at the Missouri Department of Insurance: https://insurance.mo.gov

Questions to ask any broker you interview
- Do you work with individual/sole‑proprietor clients? How many?
- Are you licensed in Missouri? Can I see your license number?
- Do you specialize in ACA marketplace plans or certain carriers?
- How are you compensated? Do you charge any fees?
- Will you help with enrollment, subsidy calculations, claims and renewals?
- Can you explain HSA eligibility and plan options for someone self‑employed?

Other issues specific to the self‑employed
- If your household income fluctuates, ask about estimating income for premium tax credits and how to adjust during the year.
- Consider HSA‑qualified high‑deductible plans if you want tax‑advantaged savings.
- If you have employees (or plan to), ask about small-group plans and QSEHRA/HRAs.

If you want, give me your ZIP code and the answers to the questions above and I’ll find and recommend 3–5 top-rated local brokers in Kansas City, MO, with contact details and pros/cons for each.
